notes:
CRM notes: shorthand from calls and POC plan. Primary ask: definitive alignment on latency SLO semantics for dedicated capacity. Workload: conversational support bot (streaming tokens) + short-hit reranking calls and periodic bulk embeddings. Requirements summary: p50/p95/p99 targets and measurement surface must be contractually defined; streaming vs non-streaming behavior must be explicit.

- Latency targets (Driftwood proposal): non-streaming (inference-only): p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 500ms. Streaming (user-facing): time-to-first-byte (TTFB) p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 350ms; time-to-final-token p95 <= 900ms for long responses (>512 tokens) but prefer per-token-rate guarantees.

- Measurement alignment ask: they want both client-side end-to-end percentiles AND server-side inference-only percentiles. Important distinctions: network/proxy overhead, SDK batching, and client aggregation windows. Driftwood insists contractual SLOs reference measurement method (e.g., 95th percentile of client-observed TTFB measured over 5-minute rolling windows), with transparent artifact: Redwood to publish both server-inference histograms and a recommended client shim to produce comparable metrics.

- Streaming-specific definitions proposed during meeting: define TTFB (first partial chunk), define initial chunk size (e.g., first N tokens or first chunk delimiter), and define per-token latency for steady-state streaming (median token delta). For p99 on streaming, measure distribution on TTFB separately from total completion; agree to exclude sessions affected by cold-starts or model loads during autoscaling events unless they exceed threshold frequency.

- Throughput/reserved planning: current target 600 RPS steady for short requests (reranking/embeddings) and 420 concurrent streaming sessions (avg 1.5 req/s per session). Estimated GPU plan: reserve 3x A100-equivalent nodes with continuous batching and KV cache pinning for conversational contexts. Redwood SE (Priya) suggested quantized 13B model variant + fallback to 7B for burst overflow; Driftwood wants fallback policy and latency hit guarantees documented.

- SLA negotiation items: uptime SLA desired 99.95% for dedicated pool; clear definition of SLO breaches (measured by region, excluding maintenance windows); request for credits formula tied to p95 violations over monthly rollup.

- Instrumentation notes: Driftwood will add client SDK timers for: request_start, ttfb_received, last_byte, total_tokens_received. They want server-side times: queue_time, decode_time, total_inference_ms. Redwood to provide mapping doc showing how server fields map to client timers.

- Open questions captured: how to contractually treat streaming partial-delivery latency vs final-response latency; whether p99 should include rare cold-starts during rolling upgrades; acceptable exclusion window definition (e.g., server-side warmup < 30s after scale event).

- Quote from Dir. of Platform: "We need guarantees we can show to Ops — not just averages. Show us what 'p95' actually means for a user on our mobile app."

- POC plan: 24h load run (na-east, eu-west) with synthetic clients for both streaming and batch workloads + joint post-mortem and SLO report. Redwood action items: deliver measurement spec, client shim, reserved GPU pricing, and fallback model latency profile.
